title: Incident budgeting experiment and SLO adoption plan — pilot + scale
content:
Purpose
This is a cross-functional experiment plan to test an "incident budgeting" approach as a lightweight mechanism to accelerate SLO adoption across product teams. Hypothesis: If teams operate with a small, explicit monthly incident budget and clear error-budget actions, we will get faster SLO alignment, reduce unplanned toil, and surface risky services earlier — without increasing alert fatigue.

Audience
- SREs, Product Eng leads, Platform, Observability, Console PMs, Solutions Eng (pilot customers), Customer Success (for impacted accounts).

Background / rationale
- We have good SLO definitions in pockets but inconsistent enforcement and little pragmatic tooling to help teams trade reliability vs. feature velocity.
- Incident budgeting = allocate a small, tracked allowance of SLO-impacting incidents (or minutes of P0/P1 downtime) per calendar month for a service. Once spent, automatic soft controls (e.g., canary gating, increased review, temporary throttling, or emergency rollbacks) kick in.
- This experiment makes the abstract concept of error budget tangible and introduces operational playbooks that teams can follow.

Goals (what success looks like)
- Pilot: three services accept budgets and run through 8 weeks of the experiment with full instrumentation.
- Metrics: 20% reduction in mean time to detection (MTTD) for pilot services, 15% reduction in MTTR, and clearer incident frequency volatility (tracked weekly).
- Adoption: blueprint and templates that enable 5 more teams to onboard in the following quarter.

Scope & constraints
- Pilot services: auth-service, realtime-routing, embeddings-cache (chosen for varied traffic patterns).
- Not in scope: network infra (hosted infra changes), customer-managed private installs.
- Budget is soft during pilot — no hard billing or punitive measures.

Experiment hypothesis and measurement plan
- Hypothesis: Explicit incident budgets will reduce reactive firefighting and encourage scheduled mitigation work (backfills, refactors).
- Primary indicators: SLO attainment percentage, incident count (P0/P1), minutes spent in degraded state, MTTR, number of follow-up corrective tickets created within 7 days after incidents.
- Secondary indicators: Pager noise (alerts/hour), number of rollbacks triggered by automatic protections, and developer sentiment (short weekly survey).

Phase plan and timeline (8 weeks pilot)
- Week -2 to 0: prep (define metrics, dashboards, select owners, runbook templates)
- Week 1: kickoff + baseline measurement collection (2 weeks of historical data pulled)
- Weeks 2–7: active experiment (apply incident budgets, enable protections, weekly status reviews)
- Week 8: retrospective, decision (adopt + scale / refine / abandon)

Roles & responsibilities (high level)
- Initiative lead: Maya Thompson (SRE) — program coordination, status, retro
- Product eng liaisons: Ethan Park (auth), Priya Menon (realtime-routing), Liam Chen (embeddings-cache) — own service onboarding and runbook updates
- Observability & dashboards: Sofia Rivera — build baseline and experiment dashboards in Console
- Platform protections & gating: Rashida Khan — implement temporary canary gating & throttles in staging for when budget is exceeded
- Customer success: TBD — advise on communication cadence for affected customers

RACI (simplified)
- Define budgets: R=Product Eng, A=SRE (Maya), C=Observability, I=Platform
- Implement protections: R=Platform, A=Platform, C=SRE, I=Product Eng
- Dashboards & alerts: R=Observability, A=Observability, C=SRE, I=Product Eng
- Retrospective & decision: R=SRE, A=VP Eng, C=product leads, I=customer success

Runbook sketch (to be turned into templates)
- Trigger: Service crosses 75% of incident budget or triggers a P1/P0
- Immediate steps: Pager escalation -> incident commander -> initial impact triage within 15 minutes
- If budget > 100%: activate soft protections (canary gate, automated traffic shift, disable non-essential features), schedule postmortem with follow-ups within 72 hours
- Post-incident: create corrective follow-up ticket, assign owner, target MTTc (mean time to closure) of 14 days for corrective work

Pilot sprint backlog (first two sprints) — owners and rough estimates
- SPRINT 0 (prep, 1 week):
  - finalize incident budget definitions (0.5d) — Maya, Ethan
  - create baseline dashboards (2d) — Sofia
  - draft runbook template (1d) — Maya
  - instrument SLO telemetry for pilot services (3d) — Priya, Liam
- SPRINT 1 (weeks 1–2):
  - enable protections in staging (~2d) — Rashida
  - run tabletop incident drill for each service (1d per service) — Product Eng + SRE
  - configure alerts and soft gates (2d) — Observability + Platform
  - create short customer comms template (0.5d) — CS / Product

Communication plan
- Weekly status email to stakeholders (SRE, Eng leads, Product, Observability) — Maya to send every Friday
- Slack channel: #sre-incident-budgeting (live log + daily check-ins)
- Bi-weekly sync with Console PM to ensure dashboard usability
- Postmortems published to Confluence with standardized template and linked to JIRA tickets

Risks and mitigations
- Risk: Teams see the budget as permission to ship riskier changes. Mitigation: emphasize governance, include gating that requires a short planned mitigation if a risky deploy is proposed and the budget is >50% used.
- Risk: Alert fatigue vs. under-alerting. Mitigation: instrument alert quality and run a weekly review of alert rationalization items.
- Risk: Production protection mechanisms cause customer-facing regressions. Mitigation: start protections in staging and run canary tests, keep protections reversible and observable.

Open questions / decisions needed
- What exact unit to budget (minutes of degraded time vs incident count vs error budget %) — propose minutes for first pilot, error % for subsequent trials.
- Who is the escalation owner when a service is cross-cutting (e.g., platform + product)? Recommend joint commander with primary owner being the service owner.
- How will non-technical SLAs (customer-facing contracts) interact with budgets? CS + legal need a short review.

Quick notes to self / working ideas (informal)
- Try 2 pilots with different budget units (auth-service: minutes; realtime-routing: incident count) to compare signal clarity.
- Use the Console "route-level SLO" view as the single source-of-truth; ensure dashboards link directly to Console pages.
- Consider a small incentive (ops time credit) for teams that stay well under budget and schedule proactive tech debt sprints.

Next steps (immediate)
- Confirm pilot service owners and get calendar invites for kickoff (Maya) — by 2026-02-20
- Sofia to publish baseline dashboards and share an access checklist — by 2026-02-24
- Platform to prepare reversible canary gating implementation document — by 2026-02-26

Appendix: quick measurement queries (examples to be converted to Console dashboards)
- weekly_incident_minutes(service)  — sum of minutes tagged P0/P1 by week
- slo_attainment(service)  — rolling 28-day percent of successful requests
- mttr_by_service(week)  — avg time from pager to resolved (hours)

End of working draft — looking for feedback on budget unit, pilot scope, and whether Platform can support reversible gating by week 2.
